content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普最近对中国的访问引起了在线航班跟踪器的特别关注。这在很大程度上是因为美国空军目前所有三架基于波音 747 的空军一号飞机——两架较旧的 VC-25A 和新的前卡塔尔 VC-25B“桥”喷气式飞机——都支持了这次旅行。另一架军用 747 飞机，即 E-4B 守夜人飞机，通常被称为“世界末日飞机”，也被发现跟踪该组织往返于亚洲。虽然这在网上引起了很多关注，包括来自国防网站的博客文章，但事实是这绝对是标准做法。 E-4B 只是总统离开该国时上演的大型空中物流芭蕾舞剧的另一部分，尽管是一个非常独特和害羞的部分。空军目前拥有四架 E-4B，也称为国家机载作战中心 (NAOC)，全部驻扎在内布拉斯加州的奥法特空军基地。其中三架飞机以 747-200 型号为基础，于 20 世纪 70 年代首次作为 E-4A 高级机载指挥所 (AACP) 投入使用。这些飞机随后在 20 世纪 80 年代达到了 E-4B NAOC 标准，并最终加入了直接改装为该配置的第四架飞机。多年来，这些喷气式飞机不断升级。
除了支持总统旅行外，守夜人飞机还定期在海外旅行期间运送国防部长（现在也称为战争部长）及其工作人员等。E-4B 守夜人喷气式飞机的库存图片。美国军方 11 月 16 日，搭载特朗普及其随行人员的 VC-25 飞机离开华盛顿特区郊外的安德鲁斯空军基地。大约在同一时间，一架 E-4B 被追踪到从奥法特起飞。特朗普首先对菲律宾进行了短暂访问，然后前往中国。飞机观察员有一个难得的机会看到所有三架 VC-25 停在马尼拉尼诺·阿基诺国际机场。美国空军：美国总统随行人员正在经安克雷奇飞往马尼拉的途中。 VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — 约翰尼·双子座(@Borrowed7Time) 2026 年 11 月 16 日 守夜人喷气式飞机分别飞往日本冲绳岛的嘉手纳空军基地。 E-4B NAOC 73-1676 在总统马尼拉之行期间停泊在嘉手纳。信用 RODN Kadena。 pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) 2026 年 11 月 17 日 今天早些时候，所有三架 VC-25 载着​​特朗普和美国代表团其他成员离开中国。当三人开始飞越日本本土时，E-4B 从嘉手纳起飞跟随他们。
美国总统返回美国 特朗普总统及其随行人员本周在结束各种会议后正在从中国返回美国的途中： VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B “TRUCK55” 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 正如开头提到的，在特朗普访问期间，E-4B 跟踪 VC-25 并在嘉手纳进行前沿部署先去菲律宾，然后去中国，这并不奇怪。这是美国总统出国旅行的标准操作程序。在特朗普五月份访华期间，飞行追踪器特别发现了类似的飞机队列。 HANK99 又名“末日飞机”(E-4B NAOC) 从内布拉斯加州奥法特空军基地飞往美国

【原文 English Original】
U.S. President Donald Trump’s recent visit to China has drawn particular attention from online flight trackers. This is in no small part due to the fact that all three of the U.S. Air Force’s current Boeing 747-based Air Force One aircraft – the two older VC-25As and the new ex-Qatari VC-25B “Bridge” jet – have supported the trip. Another militarized 747, an E-4B Nightwatch , commonly referred to as a ‘doomsday plane,’ was also spotted shadowing the group to and from Asia. While this drew a lot of attention online, including blog posts from defense-focused sites, the reality is this is absolutely standard practice. The E-4B is just another part, albeit a very unique and shy one, of the massive aerial logistics ballet that occurs whenever the President leaves the country. The Air Force currently has four E-4Bs, also known as National Airborne Operations Centers (NAOC), all based at Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska. Based on the 747-200 model, three of these planes first entered service in the 1970s as E-4A Advanced Airborne Command Posts (AACP). Those aircraft were subsequently brought up to the E-4B NAOC standard in the 1980s, and were eventually joined by a fourth example converted straight to that configuration. The jets have been continuously upgraded over the years. In addition to supporting presidential travel, the Nightwatch aircraft also regularly transport the Secretary of Defense (now also referred to as the Secretary of War) and their staff during overseas trips, among other roles. A stock picture of an E-4B Nightwatch jet. US Military The VC-25s carrying Trump and the rest of his entourage left Andrews Air Force Base just outside Washington, D.C., on November 16. An E-4B was tracked heading out from Offutt at around the same time. Trump headed first for a brief visit to the Philippines before traveling on to China. Plane spotters had a rare opportunity to see all three VC-25s parked together at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila. USAF: POTUS entourage en route to Manila via Anchorage. VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — Johnny Gemini (@Borrowed7Time) November 16, 2026 The Nightwatch jet headed separately to Kadena Air Base on the Japanese island of Okinawa. E-4B NAOC 73-1676 bedding down at Kadena during the presidential trip to Manilla. credit RODN Kadena. pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) November 17, 2026 All three VC-25s left China carrying Trump and the rest of the U.S. delegation earlier today. As the trio began to pass over Japan’s home islands, the E-4B took off from Kadena to follow them. POTUS Returning to the US President Trump and his entourage are en-route back to the US from China after various meetings this week: VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B "TRUCK55" 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) November 19, 2026 As mentioned at the start, the E-4B shadowing the VC-25s and being forward-deployed in Kadena during Trump’s visit to the Philippines and then China is no surprise. This is standard operating procedure for when the President of the United States travels abroad. Flight trackers notably caught a similar procession of aircraft during Trump’s trip to China back in May. HANK99 aka “The Doomsday Plane” (E-4B NAOC) is airborne from Offutt AFB, Nebraska to shadow POTUS on his trip to China. https://t.co/BBsq1tkC1E pic.twitter.com/Z3zpxBX9zy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) May 12, 2026 While the E-4Bs are nowhere near as luxurious as the VC-25As or the new VC-25B, they are just as capable of serving as airborne command posts, if not more so in many respects . They are unofficially referred to as ‘doomsday planes’ because they are specifically configured to provide the president and other senior military officials with a flying headquarters they can use for any and all duties, including directing nuclear strikes during the most serious crises. They are hardened against electromagnetic pulses caused by nuclear detonations and have the ability to stay airborne for days. Their very existence, at least one being on alert at all times to support the National Command Authority , is a critical component that underpins America’s nuclear deterrent. Even if an adversary destroys much of the country, an E-4 can remain airborne to order the counter-attack. With all this in mind, the E-4B fleet is key to so-called continuity of government plans , which are in place to make sure key elements of the federal government remain functional following an attack or a similarly serious contingency. As a prime example, President George W. Bush rode on one of the VC-25A Air Force One aircraft in the immediate wake of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, but there were discussions about transferring him to a Nightwatch jet . Bush ultimately decided against making the change, but an E-4B was still scrambled and orbited over Washington, D.C., for a time. This is hardly the only time a president has made use of an E-4B, or one of its predecessors, as well as command ships, as TWZ has examined in the past . September 11th, 2001 – Boeing E-4B NAOC callsign ADDIS77 scrambled from Andrews AFB. While ATC was calling them “VENUS” which is a typical callsign used at Andrews, you can hear the urgency of the pilot wanting to get airborne. The E-4 orbited over Washington DC for a while… pic.twitter.com/K61yeFY3kZ — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 The aircraft got airborne assuming for safety reasons (safer in air than on the ground) and if needed would have flown to pickup the President or next in the line of succession (Continuity of government). — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 Within this broader context, E-4Bs have been a key feature of overseas presidential travel for decades now, although they are the least visible of the presidential aerial armada. This massive airlift and logistics effort includes bringing in multiple examples of the presidential motorcade , Marine One helicopters , and various force protection assets . This involves many sorties by C-17 and C-5 cargo aircraft that cover many thousands of miles each. The videos below from Trump’s visit this week to the Philippines give a sense of just one portion of these options, albeit the most visible one, the vertical airlift component. US President Trump landing at Luneta. Impressive to see the extent of securing the safety of the most important human being on the planet. pic.twitter.com/gIXewN6Yz3 — Emil (@13thFool) November 18, 2026 Beyond its strategic command and control mission, having an E-4B positioned in the region the president is visiting during overseas trips offers a critical option for refuge and escape, as well as an additional backup aircraft to Air Force One, should any emergencies arise. The exact parameters for where the Nightwatch aircraft go are unknown, but would be based on what suitable airports are available and what potential threats and contingencies could arise. They are never seen at the same locations as Air Force One and are always separated by a distance of dozens of miles, at least, in friendly countries — close enough to be accessed by Marine One in an emergency — or generally in a region for more sensitive locales where such close proximity basing isn’t an option. It moves in shadow of AF1 everywhere it goes overseas, usually lands at another airport nearby. This is standard procedure going back decades. We see it every single overseas trip. Beyond it's strategic and COG function it acts as a refuge/escape if something really bad happens… https://t.co/nPhxPJOKMk — Tyler Rogoway (@Aviation_Intel) November 19, 2026 E-4Bs do not need to be airborne to act as command and control platforms and secure communications relay nodes, either. This further feeds into their continuity of government role. These are capabilities that can also be made available, if required, to assist the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) during major natural disasters or to help serve as command posts and communications nodes in other emergencies. The changing character of the Air Force One fleet could put new emphasis on the E-4Bs, as well as the replacement E-4C Survivable Airborne Operations Center (SAOC) jets the Air Force is now in the process of acquiring. Trump’s trip back from China has notably underscored a significant difference between the VC-25As and the new VC-25B Bridge aircraft, which is that the latter lacks aerial refueling capability. Two fully-outfitted VC-25Bs that Boeing is still in the process of converting for the Air Force will also not be capable of refueling in flight. The E-4Bs can refuel in flight, and the E-4Cs will be able to do so, as well. Coming back from China heading to DC, the new VC-25B Bridge Air Force One does not need to refuel in Alaska but the old VC-25As do. Tracking via @ADSBex pic.twitter.com/zhcdCaIRyy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) November 19, 2026 TWZ has previously explored the Air Force’s decision to axe the aerial refueling requirement for the VC-25B in detail. The ostensible logic is that the VC-25Bs are based on newer 747-8i aircraft with more capable and fuel-efficient engines than the aging 747-200-based VC-25As. The new aircraft are, as a result, capable of longer unrefueled flights, though maximum range requirements were also watered down . At the same time, in-flight refueling allows the VC-25As ( as well as the E-4Bs ) to remain aloft for days at a time. This, in turn, could be critical in a major crisis where access to secure airfields might be limited, if not completely unavailable, for a prolonged period of time. An E-4B links up with a KC-135 aerial refueling tanker. USAF The  VC-25B Bridge jet has prompted a whole new array of operational security questions, which TWZ was calling attention to even before the decision was formally made to outfit it for presidential use. The circumstances of Trump’s return from the NATO summit in Turkey in July had prompted a further flurry of reports about whether the modified, Qatari-gifted jet lacked sufficient defensive features and other capabilities in line with the existing VC-25As. The President had flown to Turkey on the Bridge jet, but was reportedly covertly moved between other aircraft on the way back. This was said to have been done as a security precaution amid then-escalating fighting with Iran . A stock picture of the VC-25B Bridge aircraft seen at the time of its official unveiling. USAF President Trump subsequently downplayed the series of events, but said that the Bridge aircraft would be sent to have its capabilities “maxed out.” The White House confirmed that the jet would receive “additional upgrades and enhancements,” but did not elaborate. It is unclear how the aircraft’s configuration has changed in the ensuing months. It is worth noting here that the upgrades in question would have to be limited to defensive systems. The Bridge aircraft could also have entered service without certain communications and networking capabilities found on the VC-25As. Another way to mitigate any such limitations could be to have a VC-25A or an E-4B operating closely enough to establish a line-of-sight data connection relatively quickly so it can leverage the better-equipped aircraft’s communications systems if needed. As an aside, Trump arrived in China aboard the Bridge aircraft and was seen boarding it to head back to the United States. Reporters onboard had their phones taken away during the return flight for still unexplained security reasons. 科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

【原文 English Original】
Satellite imagery has revealed an unusual uncrewed aircraft at Pucheng, China, with a configuration that bears very strong similarities to Boeing’s carrier-based MQ-25 Stingray . While we still have no idea about the function of the drone, the facility itself also appears to be an increasingly important hub for China’s expanding uncrewed aircraft industry . A wider-view satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor shows the mystery drone at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The drone initially attracted attention after being spotted in a satellite image of Pucheng Neifu Airport in Shaanxi Province, in northwestern China, available through Apple Maps. A separate image of the drone, where it appears on a runway, is also available through Bing Maps. TWZ subsequently obtained imagery of Pucheng from Vantor showing the uncrewed aircraft in question. what a suprise! Three UAV spotted at Pucheng on apple maps. CH-7, Jiutian and a MQ-25 like UAV. pic.twitter.com/rREqLuFAdU — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 18, 2026 spotted again on bing maps! and it's on the runway this time pic.twitter.com/xLgZetmOZf — Charles Xu (@CharlesXu091121) November 19, 2026 As well as the unidentified aircraft, imagery from Pucheng dating from April of this year also reveals what appears to be a CH-7 stealthy flying-wing drone and an example of the heavyweight jet-powered Jiutian mothership drone . A CH-7 at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor A Jiutian drone mothership at Pucheng on April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor The most obvious comparison for the unidentified aircraft is Boeing’s MQ-25 Stingray. The MQ-25 is a carrier-based uncrewed aircraft developed primarily to provide aerial refueling for U.S. Navy aircraft, extending the range and operational flexibility of carrier air wings. It also provides a foundation for future uncrewed naval aviation capabilities . In terms of dimensions, the unidentified Chinese UAV has a wingspan of approximately 66 feet and a length of 49 feet, according to Vantor. In contrast, the MQ-25 measures approximately 75 feet in wingspan and 51 feet in length. MQ-25 Stingray. Boeing The Chinese drone appears to occupy a similar general design category, but there are several important differences notable at this stage. One of the most noticeable is the forward fuselage. Unlike the MQ-25, whose forward section has a relatively flattened, shovel-like appearance, the Chinese aircraft appears to have a more conventional, tapered nose. Perhaps this could incorporate a conical radome housing radar equipment. That theory, and it is just a theory, could be supported by the different color of the nose compared to the yellow primer-painted airframe. The air intake is also different. Rather than the exotic, flush inlet associated with the MQ-25 , the Chinese design has a more conventional dorsal intake that appears serrated to help with radar signature and/or split into two channels. Another possibility is that the aircraft has two engines, although that remains speculative, based on the apparent bifurcated intake. A side-by-side look at the drone seen in the image of Pucheng, at left, and an MQ-25, offering comparative views of their inlets. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/Boeing The tail configuration may also be distinctive, with a laterally flared V-tail, like the MQ-25, but possibly incorporating visible control surfaces instead of an all-moving tailplane design. Taken together, these features suggest an aircraft that shares some of the MQ-25’s general design philosophy but is not an attempt at a direct clone. Long-time Chinese aerospace observer and TWZ contributor Andreas Rupprecht , who has been following developments surrounding the aircraft, believes China could be following a development path similar to Boeing’s, potentially producing a carrier-based uncrewed aerial refueling platform that can also undertake intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. “I think China is actually following the same path as Boeing here, and it’s heading towards a tanker that can also take on other roles as an ISR platform,” Rupprecht told us. A radar-equipped aircraft with substantial endurance could potentially perform surveillance and other sensor-related missions when not being used as a tanker. The potential development of a multirole uncrewed tanker at Pucheng would also fit into a much broader push by China to expand the role of uncrewed aircraft in its naval aviation forces. One of the most notable developments is the GJ-21 , a navalized derivative of the GJ-11 Sharp Sword stealth uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV). Featuring folding wings and provisions for catapult launches and arrested recoveries, the low-observable flying-wing design is intended to operate from China’s growing fleet of large-deck warships , including the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . In October 2026, Chinese state media reported that the GJ-21 had successfully completed its first takeoff and landing aboard the vessel, a significant milestone in the development of shipborne fixed-wing combat drones. GJ-21 carrier-based UCAV. via Chinese internet The GJ-21 effort is taking place alongside the introduction of China’s new catapult-equipped Fujian aircraft carrier, which has begun operating the J-35 stealth fighter, J-15T carrier-based fighter, and KJ-600 airborne early warning aircraft. Taken together, these developments point to an increasingly ambitious effort to integrate uncrewed aircraft into China’s future carrier air wings , potentially spanning stealthy strike platforms, surveillance systems, and other specialized support aircraft. The unidentified Pucheng aircraft could represent another, quite different part of that wider effort — or something else altogether. At the same time, this aircraft is roughly 20 percent dimensionally smaller than the MQ-25, which would mean it would have less fuel to give. It’s also worth noting that Boeing’s MQ-25 emerged from an unmanned combat air vehicle (UCAV) design that included low-observable features. Multirole UCAV concepts predating it also looked very similar. The MRE concept from Lockheed during the 1990s looks very similar to the MQ-25 we know today. (Lockheed Martin) In addition, Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), for instance, the FQ-42 Vengeance, and also the XQ-67 Off-Board Sensing Station share a similar overall design. With this in mind, and remembering its different nose section, this could just as easily be a true multirole UCAV or even a CCA, such as one designed for force protection of high-value aerial assets, and it may not even be carrier-capable. Rupprecht cautioned that the manufacturer of the mystery drone remains unidentified. However, one of the more interesting clues about the aircraft’s possible origins comes from Shenyang Aircraft Corporation (SAC). Rupprecht pointed to a propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025, which he believes could fit the development lineage of the larger aircraft now visible at Pucheng. The sub-scale propeller-driven demonstrator unveiled by SAC in 2025. The background reads (rough translation): “Rollout Ceremony for Final Assembly of Shenyang’s First ‘Surrogate Flight Test’ Pilot-Test Verification Platform UAV.” via Chinese internet A smaller, propeller-driven demonstrator could provide a relatively inexpensive way to investigate aerodynamic characteristics, autonomous flight controls, mission systems, and other technologies before progressing to a much larger aircraft. This piston-powered, propeller-driven aircraft with a broadly similar configuration to the MQ-25 was seen in a video flying, as well. 突然想起中国一家民营无人机公司，做过一款MQ-25活塞桨叶版 https://t.co/Y69dfzpLNS pic.twitter.com/IzU08PC8DK — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) November 18, 2026 Whether the Pucheng aircraft is related to this SAC demonstrator or if it’s an entirely separate program remains unknown. Beyond the external resemblance, there are no indications that they are linked, and the aircraft could just be a general test surrogate platform. The configuration isn’t totally novel in the advanced UAS world. The aircraft’s appearance is also interesting given the location where it has been spotted. Pucheng Neifu Airport is located in Shaanxi Province, and its surrounding aviation facilities include an area identified in Apple Maps as the National Aeronautics Industrial Base Pucheng General Aviation Industrial Park Guanliban. The industrial park has its own smaller runway, separate from the main airport infrastructure. A close-up of Pucheng with no drones visible, as of June 16, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 The site had remained relatively obscure to outside observers until roughly the past one to two years, according to Rupprecht. More recently, however, various aircraft manufacturers have apparently been conducting testing there. This raises the possibility that Pucheng is not simply an individual manufacturer’s flight-test location, but a facility used by multiple organizations developing and evaluating uncrewed aircraft. Rupprecht also raised the possibility that Pucheng could potentially be a specialized uncrewed aircraft testing facility associated with China’s Flight Test Establishment at Xi’an, commonly known as CFTE. “I cannot say (yet) whether this — and this is my theory — is effectively a branch of the CFTE at Xi’an, which is for crewed and this is a base for uncrewed ones,” Rupprecht explained. A satellite image provided to TWZ by Vantor provides an overview of Pucheng as of April 23, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor If Pucheng does serve as a shared testing location for multiple manufacturers, it could help explain the appearance of several otherwise unrelated UAV designs at the same site. Returning to the mystery drone, the combination of its apparent size, configuration, and possible connection to earlier Chinese demonstrator programs makes it an interesting development to watch. Regardless, for now, the imagery from Pucheng offers a glimpse of a potentially significant new Chinese uncrewed aircraft program. content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平一致认为，即使两国争夺人工智能霸主地位，人类也应该始终参与使用人工智能技术的军事决策，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周五表示。特朗普在中国深圳与习近平会面归来后，贝森特对 CNBC 表示，该协议是特朗普亚洲之行的主要成果之一。贝森特表示：“我认为，特朗普总统和习主席一致认为，人类应该始终参与情报情报机构做出的任何军事决策，并且不应允许情报情报机构在重大军事行动中自主行事，这一点非常重要。”贝森特指的是特朗普政府对该技术的首选术语“超级智能”。贝森特表示，美中就该技术的军事使用达成的协议需要人类参与和其他保障措施，不会受到两国人工智能霸主竞争的影响。他补充说，美国人工智能实验室需要保持其技术领先地位，作为抵御网络攻击中使用的“危险”中国人工智能模型的最佳防御手段。贝森特说：“但是，当双方都同意不应该在无人参与的情况下发起任何重大军事行动时，这与竞争无关。”
他表示，涉及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋和一名与他有恋情的中国公民的间谍指控并未在特习双边会晤中提及。贝森特表示，在特朗普采取他所谓的“非常强硬的路线”后，英伟达的第二级人工智能芯片 H200 仍然是中国可以通过许可购买的最先进的芯片。 “我认为我们看到的是中国人在 H200 上的订单很少，因为他们试图构建自己的芯片堆栈，而且我认为他们可能落后了很多年，”他补充道。英伟达丑闻发生后，贝森特淡化了财政部长和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在人工智能芯片限制问题上所表达的分歧，称特朗普政府官员“都致力于遵循特朗普总统的指示”。美国商务部周一采取措施，进一步限制中国获得先进人工智能芯片，包括中国实体可以租用计算能力的海外数据中心使用的芯片。 “我认为我们将会看到适当的芯片限制已经到位，并且远程访问已经被限制，”他说。

【原文 English Original】
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions that use artificial intelligence technologies, even as the two countries compete for AI supremacy , Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday. Bessent told CNBC after returning from Trump’s meeting with Xi in Shenzhen, China, that the agreement was among the major achievements of Trump’s trip to Asia. “I think it was very important that President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” Bessent said, referring to the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology, “super intelligence.” Bessent said that the U.S.-China agreement on military use of the technology, requiring human involvement and other safeguards, would not be affected by the two countries’ competition for AI supremacy. He added that U.S. AI labs needed to maintain their technological lead as the best defense against “dangerous” Chinese AI models that are being used in cyberattacks. “But there’s nothing to do with competition when it says that both sides agree that no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved,” Bessent said. He said that the spying allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese national that he was romantically involved with did not come up in the Trump-Xi bilateral meeting. Bessent said that Nvidia’s second-tier AI chip, the H200, remained the most advanced chip that China could purchase with licenses, after Trump took what he called a “very firm line.” “I think what we have seen is a paucity of orders from the Chinese on the H200s as they try to build out their own chip stack, and I think that they are probably many years behind,” he added. Bessent downplayed differences that he had voiced between the views of Treasury and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on AI chip restrictions in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, saying Trump administration officials were “all committed to following President Trump’s instructions.” The Commerce Department took steps on Monday to further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips, including those used by overseas data centers where Chinese entities can rent computing power. “I think we are going to see that the proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed,” he said.

title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动是否能够解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，特别是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

【原文 English Original】
The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

空军向数十家公司颁发了价值 16B 美元的巨额发动机工作合同 - Breaking Defense
2026 年 4 月 22 日，在与 Husets Speedway 代表进行社区参与访问期间，F-16 战隼发动机在南达科他州 Joe Foss Field 的飞机发动机测试设施中进行测试。 （美国空军国民警卫队照片由卢克·奥尔森军士长拍摄）
编者注：本文发表后，空军通知 Breaking Defense，合同授予信息发布错误。该军种正计划签署价值 161 亿美元的先进推进采购合同，但尚未这样做。单击此处了解最新信息。
华盛顿——空军今天指定了数十家公司作为一项集体合同的获奖者，该合同在未来 15 年可能价值 161 亿美元，用于“先进推进企业工作”——尽管获奖者只看到了其中的一小部分。
今天宣布的这份合同总共颁发给了 58 家供应商，每家供应商都获得了 1,000 美元的奖励。预计工作期可能会延长至 2041 年 11 月。
合同授予书上写道：“该合同规定在推进开发的所有领域和生命周期阶段持续增强推进技术。”
今年早些时候，空军透露了大型合同飞行器的机会，在行业招标中概述了“先进推进采购合同”。但据《空军与太空部队》杂志报道，三月份的一份通知称，该军种尚未为该计划获得资金，并且在获得资金之前不会颁发合同。
另一份同样在三月份发布的通知称，该计划旨在“实现适用于推进系统开发的所有领域和生命周期阶段的快速响应，包括技术成熟、概念开发、概念演示、集成、采购、生产、部署、运营和维护，以快速满足当前和未来的推进系统要求，同时最大限度地利用数字环境。”
空军没有立即回应寻求进一步澄清合同资金和预期工作范围的置评请求。
确保亚太数字战场的安全
从电子战威胁到联盟数据共享，了解美国及其盟军如何加强印太地区的数字战场。
该合同的获奖者包括一系列公司，从初创公司到老牌发动机公司，通知称这些公司都是经过竞争挑选的。由于合同的结构为无限期交付、无限数量，空军不一定有义务花费全部金额。
该奖项颁发之际，空军正在寻求新的、更有效的方法来为其现有和未来的平台（从无人机僚机到大型机动飞机）提供动力。该服务最近聘请了多家供应商，为不同尺寸的无人机和导弹提供选择，并且还在开发一种先进的发动机，可为 F-47 隐形战斗机等未来平台提供动力。

An F-16 Fighting Falcon engine is tested in the aircraft engine test facility at Joe Foss Field, South Dakota, April 22, 2026, during a community engagement visit with representatives from Husets Speedway. (U.S. Air National Guard photo by Master Sgt. Luke Olson)
Editor’s note: After publication of this story, the Air Force informed Breaking Defense that the contract award was posted in error. The service is planning to issue the $16.1 billion Advanced Propulsion Acquisition Contract, but has not yet done so. Click here for the latest.
WASHINGTON — The Air Force today named dozens of companies as awardees for a group contract potentially worth $16.1 billion over the next 15 years for “advanced propulsion enterprise work” — though the winners are only seeing a small fraction of that to start.
The contract, announced today, was issued to a total of 58 vendors, who have each been awarded $1,000. The expected work period could stretch to November 2041.
“This contract provides for the continuing enhancement of propulsion technology across all areas and lifecycle phases of propulsion development,” the contract award reads.
The Air Force earlier this year revealed the opportunity for the large contract vehicle, outlining an “Advanced Propulsion Acquisition Contract” in industry solicitations. But a March notice stated the service had not yet secured funding for the initiative, and would not issue contracts until doing so, according to Air & Space Forces Magazine.
Another notice, also posted in March, said the initiative is meant to “enable[] a rapid response applicable to all areas and lifecycle phases of propulsion development, including technology maturation, concept development, concept demonstrations, integration, procurement, production, fielding, operations, and sustainment to quickly meet current and future propulsion system requirements, while maximizing the use of the digital environment.”
The Air Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment seeking further clarity on the contract’s funding and expected scope of work.
Securing the Asia-Pacific digital battlespace
From electronic warfare threats to coalition data sharing, discover how US and allied forces are strengthening the digital battlespace across the Indo-Pacific.
The contract’s awardees encompass a range of firms, from startups to established engine primes, who the notice says were each competitively picked. Structured as an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract, the Air Force is not necessarily obligated to spend the full amount.
The award comes as the Air Force seeks new and more effective ways to power its existing and future platforms, from drone wingmen to large mobility aircraft. The service has recently tapped several vendors to open up options for different sizes of drones and missiles, and is also developing an advanced engine that could power future platforms like the F-47 stealth fighter.

Australia—Tomahawk Capability Development
The Government of Australia has requested to buy Theater Mission Planning Center (TMPC) and associated communications systems; TMPC Mission Planning System (MPS); program management; engineering, training, and logistics services to support the development, procurement, and delivery of the MPS; and other related elements of logistics and program support. The estimated total cost is $300 million.
This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States. Australia is one of our most important allies in the Western Pacific. The strategic location of this political and economic power contributes significantly to ensuring peace and economic stability in the Western Pacific. It is vital to the U.S. national interest to assist our ally in developing and maintaining a strong and ready self-defense capability.
This proposed sale will improve Australia's capability to meet current and future threats by enhancing its Tomahawk capability, strengthening its ability to deter regional threats, and improving its homeland defense. Australia will improve its interoperability with U.S. maritime forces and other allied forces as well as its ability to contribute to missions of mutual interest. Australia will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces.
The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the basic military balance in the region.
The principal contractors will be BAE Systems, located in San Diego, CA; Tapestry Solutions, located in St. Louis, MO; Peraton, located in San Jose, CA; and Leidos, located in Virginia Beach, VA. At this time, the U.S. Government is not aware of any offset agreement proposed in connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between the purchaser and the contractor.
Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor representatives to Australia.
There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed sale.

The Tomahawk mission planning capability contains sensitive technology, hardware, and software that enhances the operational employment of the Tomahawk Land Attack Missile.
2. The highest level of classification of defense articles, components, and services included in this potential sale is TOP SECRET/SENSITIVE COMPARTMENTED INFORMATION.
3. If a technologically advanced adversary were to obtain knowledge of the specific hardware and software elements, the information could be used to develop countermeasures that might reduce system effectiveness or be used in the development of a system with similar or advanced capabilities.
4. A determination has been made that Australia can provide substantially the same degree of protection for the sensitive technology being released as the U.S. Government. This proposed sale is necessary in furtherance of the U.S. foreign policy and national security objectives outlined in the Policy Justification.
5. All defense articles, technical data, and services listed in this transmittal have been authorized for release and export to the Government of Australia.

中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际国防和航空航天史上最重要的活动之一，成为中国快速发展的航空和军事工业的主要公开展示地。两年一度的中国国际航空航天展览会（俗称中国航展）于 1996 年首次举办，为展示中国一些最先进的军事硬件提供了难得的机会，其中包括在其他地方很少如此详细展示的飞机和系统。虽然该活动也是中国航空航天工业向潜在国际客户推广其产品的主要平台，但它日益成为展示新军事能力和提供难以评估的项目的重要场所。
第十五届中国国际航空航天展览会（又称 2024 年中国航展）于 2024 年 11 月 15 日在中国广东省珠海市中国国际航空航天展览中心举行。摄影：VCG/VCG via Getty Images 前几届已经取得了一些特别重大的进展。 2016 年的展会上，J-20 隐形战斗机首次公开飞行亮相，而 2018 年的展会则以不同寻常的方式展示了这架飞机，包括展示其装载空对空导弹的内部武器舱。 2022年的展会上，歼20首次在珠海进行静态展示，同时还有运20重型运输机、直20直升机以及在展会上进行首次飞行演示的运20空中加油机。最近，2024 年的展会特别引人注目的是 J-35A 隐形战斗机的公开亮相和具有弹射能力的 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机的出现。一架 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机在 2024 年中国航展上进行飞行表演。CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images 今年的展览定于 12 月 7 日至 13 日举行，除其他外，将展示中国海军的广泛能力，特别强调其舰载航空能力的快速发展，这一点我们过去已经详细讨论过。
预计将亮相的最引人注目的飞机包括 J-15T 舰载战斗机、作战型 J-35 隐形战斗机、KJ-600 舰载机载预警和控制 (AEW&C) 飞机、Z-20 直升机的几种海军型号，也许最重要的是新型 JL-15 舰载教练机，它是陆基 JL-10 的发展型。JL-15 舰载教练机的照片突出显示了制动钩和弹射器发射杆。虽然我们之前在珠海见过 J-15T，但如果它配备国产 WS-10H2 发动机，将会引起特别的兴趣。这样的配置将让人们更仔细地了解中国舰载侧卫衍生产品的最新演变

【原文 English Original】
China’s People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) says it’s preparing a major presence at the upcoming 16th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition in Zhuhai, with warships , carrier-based aircraft , advanced weapons systems, and uncrewed platforms set to feature prominently. The expanded naval component will include a new maritime equipment exhibition area at Gaolan Port, located just on the other side of the bay, marking the first time the PLAN has established such a dedicated display at the event. Zhuhai has become one of the most important events on the international defence and aerospace calendar, serving as China’s principal public showcase for its rapidly developing aviation and military industries. First held in 1996, the biennial China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China, provides an unusual opportunity to see some of the country’s most advanced military hardware, including aircraft and systems that are rarely shown in such detail elsewhere. While the event also serves as a major platform for China’s aerospace industry to promote its products to potential international customers , it has increasingly become an important venue for revealing new military capabilities and offering glimpses of programs that are otherwise difficult to assess. A general view of the 15th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, or Airshow China 2024, at the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition Center on November 15, 2024, in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province of China. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Previous editions have produced some particularly significant developments. The 2016 show saw the J-20 stealth fighter make its first public flying appearance , while the 2018 edition provided an unusually revealing look at the aircraft, including a demonstration of its internal weapons bays, loaded with air-to-air missiles . The 2022 exhibition featured the J-20 on static display for the first time at Zhuhai, alongside the Y-20 heavy transport aircraft, Z-20 helicopter, and YY-20 aerial refueling tanker, which made its first flying demonstration at the event. More recently, the 2024 exhibition was particularly notable for the public debut of the J-35A stealth fighter and the appearance of the catapult-capable J-15T carrier-based fighter. A J-15T carrier-based fighter conducts a flight demonstration at Airshow China 2024. CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images This year’s exhibition, scheduled to take place from December 7 to 13, will showcase, among others, a broad range of the PLAN’s capabilities, with a particularly notable emphasis on the rapid evolution of its carrier aviation capabilities, something we have addressed in detail in the past . Among the most noteworthy aircraft expected to feature are the J-15T carrier-based fighter, the operational J-35 stealth fighter, the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft, several naval variants of the Z-20 helicopter, and, perhaps most significantly, the new JL-15 carrier-capable trainer, a development of the land-based JL-10 . A photo of the JL-15 carrier-capable trainer with the arrestor hook and catapult launch bar highlighted. Chinese internet via X While we have seen the J-15T at Zhuhai before, the aircraft will be of particular interest if it is shown with the indigenous WS-10H2 engine. Such a configuration would offer a closer look at the latest evolution of China’s carrier-based Flanker derivative and its ongoing transition toward a more domestically supported carrier aviation ecosystem. The appearance of the J-35 would be another major highlight. The aircraft represents a significant step in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ambitions, bringing a fifth-generation stealth fighter capability into the carrier air wing. Its presence would provide another opportunity to examine the progress of China’s next-generation naval fighter program. Back in 2014, Zhuhai saw the public debut of the FC-31 fighter demonstrator. At the time, it was still a land-based concept, and export was the main talking point, although there was already speculation about a naval variant, today’s J-35. A People’s Liberation Army Navy J-35 fighter during trials from the carrier Fujian last year. Chinese internet via X Meanwhile, the KJ-600 is arguably one of the most important developments in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ecosystem. The twin-engine turboprop aircraft is designed to provide airborne early warning and battle management capabilities, something that would transform the situational awareness and coordination available to China’s carrier strike groups. One of the first high-definition photos of the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft. Chinese internet via X Several variants of the Z-20 family are also expected to feature, reflecting the growing importance of helicopters in carrier operations, including airborne anti-submarine warfare, utility, and other maritime support missions. You can read more about the Z-20 family and other Chinese rotary-wing developments in this previous TWZ deep-dive on the topic . A Z-20F, the anti-submarine warfare variant of the naval Z-20 family. Three more naval Z-20s are seen in the hangar behind, including a Z-20J shipborne transport and assault variant. Chinese internet via X Perhaps the most intriguing aircraft on the list, however, is the JL-15. The JL-15 is derived from the Hongdu JL-10, also exported as the L-15 Falcon, a twin-engine advanced jet trainer and lead-in fighter trainer. The navalized development was initially reported to be designated JL-10J, but is now confirmed as being the JL-15. A tailhook-equipped mockup was spotted alongside the aircraft carrier Fujian in 2024. However, its operational status remains unclear, and China is known to have encountered difficulties with its earlier JL-9G naval trainer, whose tailhook was reportedly deleted following structural problems. Regarding the rumoured JL-10J carrier-capable jet trainer, another hint was spotted next to the carrier Fujian: It appears to be an unfinished JL-10J mockup stored on the dockside . So question is: Two tails as shown in the latest CG or just one like the regular JL-10? pic.twitter.com/BM8W8MRGWK — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) March 19, 2024 Its appearance would provide a particularly interesting indication of how China is thinking about training its next generation of carrier-based pilots. A carrier-capable development of the JL-10 would be an important addition to the emerging carrier aviation ecosystem, bridging the gap between conventional jet training and the demanding requirements of operating from an aircraft carrier. The JL-15 also makes an interesting comparison with the U.S. Navy’s somewhat stuttering efforts to introduce a new training jet for its carrier pilots. The U.S. Navy’s Undergraduate Jet Training System (UJTS) program is intended to replace its aging fleet of T-45 Goshawk trainers, but the acquisition effort has encountered considerable difficulties. Earlier this month, we described how Sierra Nevada Corporation (SNC) withdrew its proposed clean-sheet Freedom Jet from the competition, citing concerns over the Navy’s insistence on firm-fixed-price production commitments before the aircraft’s design had sufficiently matured. This leaves the Beechcraft M-346N , based on Leonardo’s established M-346 Master , as the only publicly known remaining contender . The program has also experienced schedule slippage, with the initial contract award now expected in the fourth quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Perhaps more significant is the difference in the two services’ approaches to carrier aviation training. The U.S. Navy has removed the requirement for its next-generation jet trainer to be capable of operating from an actual aircraft carrier, including carrier qualification and simulated carrier touch-and-goes at land-based facilities. Instead, it increasingly relies on advanced simulation, virtualized training, and assisted carrier landing technologies to prepare pilots for the demands of carrier operations. The JL-15, by contrast, is intended to support carrier-based pilot training. A dedicated carrier-capable trainer could offer China a more direct pathway for preparing pilots for operations aboard its increasingly sophisticated — and expanding — carrier fleet. Taken together, the PLAN aircraft being lined up for Zhuhai this year illustrate the increasingly sophisticated and integrated nature of China’s carrier aviation ambitions . As well as the aircraft carriers and their embarked aircraft, these ambitions also require other surface and subsurface vessels to operate effectively. Uncrewed systems will form another important part of the display. The exhibition will include aerial drones, uncrewed underwater vehicles, and other autonomous platforms, reflecting the PLAN’s growing interest in the potential of uncrewed warfare. Chinese media reports suggest that the WZ-2 uncrewed helicopter will receive its public debut at Zhuhai, while the PLAN may well also want to capitalize on its recent announcement that it had successfully launched and recovered a GJ-21 stealthy flying-wing uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . GJ-21. Chinese internet via X A chance to see the GJ-21 up close would be a huge deal, but there are many other naval drone options that could be revealed in more detail. There are likely to be more navalized collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) concepts and developments, especially since the adoption of the electromagnetic aircraft launch system (EMALS) catapult opens up a huge range of possibilities for uncrewed aircraft operating as part of a carrier air wing. Potentially, these could include the mysterious MQ-25-like drone that we recently discussed , the role of which remains unclear. On top of that, constant CCA testing at locations such as Malan suggests there could be much more to discuss than just the systems officially highlighted. Many other naval drones will surely be on display as well, including lower-end attritable concepts. Beyond static displays, China’s navy plans to organize flight demonstrations, formation flights, and simulated operational exercises. Its stated aim is to highlight not only the capabilities of individual platforms but also their ability to operate together in complex maritime environments. Photos have emerged showing apparent rehearsals for the display, presenting examples of the J-15, J-35, and KJ-600 to represent Beijing’s broader carrier air wing ecosystem. Two J-15s, two J-35s, and a KJ-600 purportedly taking part in a rehearsal for a formation fly-over at Zhuhai. Chinese internet via X It is not immediately clear which versions of the J-15 are participating in this formation flight: they could be J-15Ts, but another possibility is the electronic warfare version, the J-15DT , that we have profiled in the past. Regardless, they highlight how China’s carrier aviation ambitions are increasingly focused on catapult-assisted takeoff but arrested recovery (CATOBAR) operations, which offer many advantages . The J-15DT electronic warfare version of the Chinese carrier Flanker is outfitted for operations aboard catapult-equipped flattops like the Fujian . Chinese internet via X For the first time, the exhibition will also include a substantial surface fleet component, making use of the docks at the nearby Gaolan Port. Among the vessels expected to be featured are the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, the Type 055 guided-missile destroyer, and the Type 054A guided-missile frigate. Their presence will offer a public-facing showcase of China’s increasingly sophisticated surface fleet and its expanding range of maritime capabilities. It should also be recalled that it was at Gaolan Port where at least one Chinese uncrewed surface vessel , a distinctive trimaran craft, was first spotted. The Type 055 guided-missile destroyer Nanchang sails during the naval exercise Joint Sea-2021 on October 19, 2021, in the Western part of the Pacific Ocean. Photo by Sun Zifa/China News Service via Getty Images The broader messaging surrounding the exhibition is also notable. According to the PLAN, this year’s displays will place greater emphasis on operational readiness and training, with active-duty equipment that regularly participates in exercises and maritime security missions taking precedence over purely exhibition-oriented displays. This should underscore how Beijing has rapidly spun up its naval capabilities, introducing new and more capable equipment that is increasingly capable of more sustained out-of-area operations. The expanded naval presence at Zhuhai looks set to provide a substantial public showcase of China’s ongoing naval modernization. As well as the combination of the J-15T, J-35, KJ-600, and Z-20 variants, the JL-15 points to an increasingly comprehensive carrier aviation enterprise. And, judging by previous editions of the show, there will almost certainly be more novelties on display as well. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow appeared first on TWZ .

content:
台湾新北市——分析人士称，中国的第四艘航空母舰是一艘迄今为止被称为 004 型的巨型舰艇，最早将于明年面世，其尺寸将比前几艘航母更大，并且配备核动力，在发生任何冲突时可以比平常更快地起飞飞机。这可能会增加日本和美国等已经对中国军队保持高度戒备的国家的压力。智库国防优先事项亚洲项目主任表示，目前正在北方港口城市大连建造的这艘航母部署后可容纳 75 至 90 架飞机。据智库战略与国际研究中心 (CSIS) 称，截至 10 月，该船的船体从未完工的船头到船尾长约 322 米，宽约 46 米。 CSIS 称 004 型“比中国海军任何其他级别的水面战舰都要大得多”。新加坡南洋理工大学高级研究员科林·许 (Collin Koh) 表示，该航母的航拍照片显示“基本船体形式”已经建成，这预示着 2027 年发射的良好前景。他说，部署需要五到十年的时间。相关军事专家表示，自2025年政治争端以来，中国已在日本附近的海军存在“正常化”，考虑到其规模，包括海岸警卫队船只和海军军舰在内的庞大中国舰队可能已经瞄准了台湾的海上邻国日本。
Koh表示，这些规格将使004型航母比目前中国舰队中最大的一艘——中国的福建号航母“略大”。台北战略与兵棋推演研究委员会主席亚历山大·黄(Alexander Huang)表示，目前获得的有关004型航母的信息——可能会以中国现有的三艘航母等省份的名字重新命名——从电子设备、吨位和飞机运载能力方面将这艘航母归类为“超级航母”。 Koh说，机载核动力将为飞机提供比中国现有的电磁飞机发射系统更多的推进力。他表示，这将消除航母上对发电机的需求，同时允许更快的起飞（不影响有效载荷）和快速的战斗周转以加油。 “这似乎标志着某种战略目标，”高在谈到核能力时说道。 “它不仅仅会沿着你的海岸移动。它似乎标志着某种全球野心。”康奈尔大学专门研究军事历史和国防政策的教授大卫·西尔贝表示，核动力将使航母“基本上具有无限的续航力”，并允许在全球部署，而无需常规动力航母所需的加油机支持。黄说，第四艘航母可能会部署到中国北方，因为其他三艘航母都在南方。
他说，在这种情况下，中国可以“利用这四种方式中的一种来始终在某个地方开展活动”。黄补充道，004型航母可能用于训练、维护以及作战。分析人士表示，中国的第四艘航母使其更接近与美国海军的竞争。西尔贝说，它的尺寸将与美国尼米兹级和福特级航母相当，这意味着它可以搭载多达 100 架飞机。 “这使得它比以前只能运载 50 架左右的航母具有更强的攻击力，”他说。美国海军拥有 11 艘航母，全部为核动力。高说，即使规模小于美国舰队，拥有核动力航母的中国海军也可以对美国构成挑战。美国海军在关岛保留基地

【原文 English Original】
NEW TAIPEI CITY, Taiwan — China’s fourth aircraft carrier, a gigantic vessel known so far as just Type 004, will come out as early as next year bigger than its predecessors and with nuclear power that can launch planes faster than usual in case of any conflict, analysts say. And it’s tipped to add pressure on countries, such as Japan and the United States, that already keep a high alert for the Chinese military. The carrier being built now in the northern port city Dalian could accommodate 75 to 90 planes once deployed, the Asia program director at the think tank Defence Priorities has said. As of October, the vessel’s hull measured about 322 meters in length from the unfinished bow to stern with a width of approximately 46 meters, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), also a think tank. CSIS called Type 004 “far larger than any other class of surface combatant” in China’s navy. Aerial photos of the carrier show the “basic hull form” already built, auguring well for a 2027 launch, said Collin Koh, a senior fellow at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. Deployment would take five to 10 years, he said. Related China has ‘normalized’ naval presence near Japan since political spat of 2025 Given its scale, the massive Chinese flotilla that included coast guard vessels alongside navy warships may have had Taiwan’s maritime neighbor Japan in its sights, military experts say. The specs would make Type 004 “slightly larger” than China’s Fujian aircraft carrier, currently the biggest one in its fleet, Koh said. Information available today about the Type 004 – likely to be renamed after a Chinese province like the existing three – classify the vessel as a “supercarrier” in terms of electronics, tonnage and aircraft carrying capacity, said Alexander Huang, chairman of the Council of Strategic and Wargaming Studies in Taipei. Nuclear power on board would offer the aircraft more propulsion than China’s existing electromagnetic aircraft launch system, Koh said. He said that would eliminate the need for power generators on board the carrier while allowing faster takeoffs – without payload compromises – and quick combat turnarounds for refueling. “It seems to signal a certain strategic objective,” Koh said of the nuclear capability. “It’s not just going to move along your coast. It seems to signal a certain global ambition.” Nuclear power will give the carrier “essentially unlimited endurance” and allow for global deployment without the kind of tanker support a conventionally powered carrier needs, said David Silbey, a Cornell University professor specializing in military history and defense policy. The fourth carrier may get posted to northern China because the other three are in the south, Huang said. In that scenario, he said, China could “use one of the four to always operate somewhere.” Type 004 may be used for training and maintenance as well as operations, Huang added. China’s fourth carrier gets it closer to rivaling the U.S. navy, analysts said. It will compare in size to the Nimitz and Ford class U.S. carriers, which means it can carry as many as 100 aircraft, Silbey said. “That gives it much more striking power than previous carriers, which could only carry around 50,” he said. The U.S. navy has 11 carriers, all nuclear powered. Even if smaller than the U.S. fleet, a Chinese navy with nuclear-powered carriers can mount a challenge to the United States, Koh said. The U.S. navy maintains bases in Guam, Hawaii and Japan plus treaty alliances with Japan and the Philippines. The U.S. and China have long seen each other as rival superpowers. Experts have said China sent an especially large number of its naval deployments near Japan’s southernmost islands and nearby waters since a political rift that erupted in November 2025 over a remark by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The Philippines is embroiled in a maritime sovereignty dispute with China. China plans to build more carriers over the next decade for a “blue water capability that they’ve never really had before,” Silbey said. “In the Pacific, it means that they can go after American assets that are out of range of their other assets.”

summary: 几天前，在黄仁勋承认与一名所谓的中国间谍有染后辞职后，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特表示，任何新的英伟达首席执行官都应该“来自公司外部”，但现在美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特又说黄仁勋是外部人士，这似乎为他的回归铺平了道路。当时，贝森特的主张与美国总统的主张形成鲜明对比，特朗普呼吁黄仁勋复职。今天早些时候，特朗普在他的 Truth Social 账户上发表了一篇文章，表示他“希望”英伟达董事会重新聘用黄仁勋。
content:
几天前，在黄仁勋承认与一名所谓的中国间谍有染后辞职后，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特表示，任何新的英伟达首席执行官都应该“来自公司外部”，但现在美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特又说黄仁勋是外部人士，这似乎为他的回归铺平了道路。当时，贝森特的主张与美国总统的主张形成鲜明对比，特朗普呼吁黄仁勋复职。今天早些时候，特朗普在他的 Truth Social 账户上发表了一篇文章，表示他“希望”英伟达董事会重新聘用黄仁勋。现在，贝森特已经同意了，尽管此前他曾呼吁英伟达进行“戏剧性改组”。贝森特的最新评论是在哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对国家”节目中发表的。当被问及英伟达在寻找新首席执行官而不是让黄仁勋回来时是否应该考虑目前的薪资之外时，贝森特辩称，他“说他们应该去外面，但他现在在外面。”贝森特还表示，他“假设[黄]不知道[爱丽丝黄]是一名所谓的间谍”。迄今为止，这一点尚未得到公开证实。 *BESSENT：我们已经与 $NVDA 临时管理层、主要董事及其律师取得了联系，我们确实需要答案*BESSENT：我说他们应该到外面去，JENSEN 现在在外面。我们将看看企业的哪个级别知道，它是否一直到最高层*贝森特：我们将看看他们要说什么。
对于这种规模的交易，不存在无法追踪的握手交易*BESSENT：我假设他不知道她是一名被指控的间谍 2026 年 11 月 22 日 Bessent 的最新声明可能是与特朗普重新结盟的语义，但目前尚不清楚他们中的任何一个是否会影响已经表示无意的 Nvidia 董事会尽管同一董事会的一些成员仍在寻求允许黄重返公司，但他还是与黄双双受惠。不出所料，黄已经表示他将“荣幸”回归，但现在的情况已经超出了与 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 的简单恋情。事实上，现在可能已经揭露了多项事务，这对他的案件没有任何帮助，也不会在 12 月初被拖到众议院外交事务、情报和中国特别委员会面前。在有消息称，针对 Nvidia 的前客户、Alice Huang 工作的公司 Megaspeed 是否参与绕过 AI 芯片出口管制的消息展开刑事调查后，Nvidia 的顶级律师也必须露面。 Megaspeed 长期以来一直被指控参与芯片走私活动。 2025 年 10 月的一项调查发现，该公司通过进口和再出口流程帮助将价值约 20 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国。
被指控的中国间谍 Alice Huang 是 Megaspeed 的一名高管，据报道，在与时任 Nvidia 首席执行官 Jensen Huang 的三年关系期间，她在进口价值超过 75 亿美元的 Nvidia AI GPU 方面发挥了重要作用。

After saying just days ago that any new Nvidia CEO should "come from outside the company" following the resignation of Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy , U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has now backtracked by saying that Huang is on the outside, seemingly paving the way for his return. At the time, Bessent's assertion was in stark contrast with that of the U.S. President, with Trump calling for Huang to be reinstated . Trump earlier today doubled down, writing of his "hope" that Nvidia's board would rehire Huang in a post on his Truth Social account. Now, Bessent has fallen in line despite having previously called for a "dramatic shake-up" at Nvidia. Bessent's latest comments came on CBS' Face the Nation show. When asked about whether Nvidia should look beyond its current payroll when looking for a new CEO instead of bringing Huang back, Bessent argued that he "said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now." Bessent also said that he would "assume [Huang] didn't know that [Alice Huang] was an alleged spy." That has, to date, not been publicly confirmed. *BESSENT: WE'VE BEEN IN TOUCH WITH $NVDA TEMPORARY MANAGEMENT, THE LEAD DIRECTORS AND THEIR LAWYERS, AND WE DO NEED ANSWERS*BESSENT: I SAID THEY SHOULD GO TO THE OUTSIDE, JENSEN IS ON THE OUTSIDE NOW. WE WILL SEE WHICH LEVEL OF THE BUSINESS KNEW, DID IT GO ALL THE WAY TO THE TOP*BESSENT: WE'LL SEE WHAT THEY HAVE TO SAY. FOR DEALS THAT SIZE THERE'S NO SUCH THING AS AN UNTRACEABLE HANDSHAKE DEAL*BESSENT: I ASSUME HE DIDN'T KNOW THAT SHE WAS AN ALLEGED SPY November 22, 2026 Bessent's latest statement may be semantics to realign himself with Trump, but it's unclear whether either of them will sway an Nvidia board that has already said it has no intention of double-dipping with Huang. That's despite some members of the same board angling for Huang to be allowed back into the company. Predictably, Huang has made it known that he would be "honored" to return , but the situation has now moved beyond a simple affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. The fact that multiple affairs may now have been uncovered won't help his case, nor will being dragged before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees in early December. Nvidia's top lawyer will also have to make an appearance following the news that a criminal investigation has been launched into whether Megaspeed — a previous client of Nvidia, and the company where Alice Huang worked — was involved in the bypassing of AI chip export controls. Megaspeed has long been accused of being involved in a chip smuggling operation. An investigation found in October 2025 that it had helped move around $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips into China via an import and re-export process. The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was a Megaspeed executive and was reportedly instrumental in the import of more than $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI GPU imports during a three-year relationship with the then Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

华盛顿——空军发言人告诉《Breaking Defense》，空军正在收回一项错误的授予价值高达 161 亿美元的大型推进工程合同车辆的公告。
11 月 20 日，空军宣布已选择 58 家公司参与该军种的先进推进采购合同 (APAC)，该合同将持续到 2041 年。该项目的结构为无限期交付、无限期数量合同，这意味着空军不一定有义务花掉全部金额。
空军发言人今天证实，五角大楼每日合同综述上发布的该合同是错误发布的，尽管该部门计划最终授予该合同。在向 Breaking Defense 披露后，五角大楼随后在 11 月 23 日的奖励公告清单中注意到了更正。
美国空军在给《Breaking Defense》的一份声明中表示：“一旦授予，APAC 将作为灵活的企业级合同工具，满足所有生命周期阶段的推进需求，包括科学和技术、研发、测试和评估、生产、维护和现代化。”
空军还确认，到目前为止，计划选择总共 58 家供应商，并向每家供应商支付 1,000 美元的初始费用，将“支持”获奖者参加颁奖后的迎新会议。
声明中写道：“随着需求得到验证和资助，未来的订单将在合格的供应商池中竞争。具体的平台、范围、资金、合同类型、履约期限和定价将在单个交付订单或任务订单级别上确定。”
11 月 20 日合同通知中的供应商池包含一系列公司，从初创公司到拥有不同推进专业知识的老牌发动机公司。该奖项颁发之际，美国空军正在寻求新的、更有效的方法来为其现有和未来的平台（从无人机僚机到大型机动飞机）提供动力。
